body.description: Creatives criteria-search response, LinkedIn Marketing API 202609. Verified against the Microsoft Learn page served as moniker li-lms-2026-09 (last updated 2026-06-24, ms.date 2026-06-19) and against live 202609 responses on 2026-10-07. The URL is relative to https://api.linkedin.com/rest/. {id} is the numeric ad account id. {campaign_urns} stands for the comma-separated campaign URNs of one request: each URN is URL-encoded as urn%3Ali%3AsponsoredCampaign%3A{cid}, while the List( ) parentheses and the commas between URNs stay literal; the Rest.li value is never percent-encoded as a whole. The page documents no maximum list length; the client sends at most 100 campaign URNs per request. intendedStatuses is an addition to the plan's request (q, campaigns, pageSize): the page documents that CANCELED creatives are hidden when querying all creatives under a campaign, and a hidden creative would drop its spend and leads from white-paper attribution and leave the creative table incomplete. A live check on 2026-10-07 returned a CANCELED creative with and without the parameter; the client sends the full list so the result never depends on that server default. The status list in request.url must equal connectors/linkedin/parser.py CREATIVE_INTENDED_STATUSES exactly, in the same order. The page's creative-id search sample mentions an X-RestLi-Method: FINDER header; live 202609 criteria searches return 200 without it, and the client does not send it. Paging: the client sends pageSize=100 (the documented maximum) and sends metadata.nextPageToken back as pageToken until a response carries no non-null nextPageToken (an absent or null token ends enumeration). On the last page live responses return an empty metadata object plus a legacy paging block that the client ignores. The page also limits an ad account to 15,000 creatives and a campaign to 100. Canonical form identity: leadgenCallToAction.destination is urn:li:adForm:{id}, and connectors/linkedin/parser.py canonical_form_urn maps it to urn:li:leadGenForm:{id} with the same id; the Lead Sync migration guide states that the form id "is still the unique identifier of the form", and on 2026-10-07 every live adForm destination id matched a lead form returned by leadForms under that id. That canonical URN is stored as creative.lead_form_urn and joins the content-asset registry, so every version of a form maps to the same white paper. Headline and intro text come from the referenced post through posts.json, not from this surface. Undeclared keys fail validation, so a field a newer version adds must be declared here before a capture containing it can pass. documented_sample is the page's criteria search sample response, verbatim. Its nextPageToken is the page's public sample cursor, not a credential: a secret-scan match on it is settled by an exact-value allowlist entry in .gitleaks.toml, never by editing the sample.

elements.description: One page of creatives matching the campaigns and intendedStatuses criteria, sorted by creative id (ASCENDING unless sortOrder is sent, which the client does not do).

items.description: One creative. parse_creative stores it in the creative table: id, campaign, account, name, intendedStatus (normalised through CREATIVE_STATUS_MAP), content.reference as post_urn, leadgenCallToAction.destination as the canonical lead_form_urn and leadgenCallToAction.label as cta_label. Required keys are those present in every documented and live element that parse_creative needs; everything else is optional, and live responses omit an optional field rather than sending null.

id.description: Sponsored creative URN, urn:li:sponsoredCreative:{id}. A string URN in every sample and live response, never a bare number. Read-only.

name.description: Advertiser-set creative name. Absent when none was set (observed live).

intendedStatus.description: Creative intended status, set independently of the parent campaign's status; the parent status overrides it in effect. Values as listed on the served page. The page documents that CANCELED creatives are hidden from campaign searches unless intendedStatuses is sent; REMOVED creatives stay fetchable because performance data exists.

content.description: Sponsored content. A union: the product reads only reference, a post URN (urn:li:share:{id} or urn:li:ugcPost:{id}; urn:li:adInMailContent:{id} for message ads). Other variants (event ad, document ad, text ad, spotlight, follower, job and third-party VAST video ads) carry their own keys that the product does not read, so undeclared keys are allowed here.

reference.description: URN of the sponsored post or InMail content.

inlineContent.description: Inline post payload, documented for action=createInline. Not seen in live criteria searches; declared so a response carrying it validates. Not read by the product.

dynamicContent.description: Undocumented dynamic-content override observed live on 2026-10-07 (for example value.video.dynamicCommentaryOverride). Declared so real responses validate; not read by the product.

leadgenCallToAction.description: Lead-gen call to action, required on the platform for LEAD_GENERATION campaigns. No page sample carries this node, so it is declared from the page's LeadgenCreativeCallToAction schema table; live responses match it. destination is an ad form URN, urn:li:adForm:{id}, immutable once the creative leaves DRAFT; its canonical form urn:li:leadGenForm:{id} (same id) joins the content-asset registry. label is the call-to-action label that open-rate tests change.

label.description: Call-to-action button label, as listed on the served page.

isTest.description: True for a creative under a test account. The flag is isTest, not test.

isServing.description: Whether the creative is currently serving. Read-only.

servingHoldReasons.description: Reasons the creative is not serving; absent while it serves. Open strings, so a new reason never rejects a real response. Documented values: STOPPED, UNDER_REVIEW, REJECTED, FORM_HOLD, PROCESSING, PROCESSING_FAILED, REFERRED_CONTENT_QUALITY_HOLD, JOB_POSTING_ON_HOLD, JOB_POSTING_INVALID, CAMPAIGN_STOPPED, ACCOUNT_TOTAL_BUDGET_HOLD, ACCOUNT_END_DATE_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_START_DATE_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_END_DATE_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_TOTAL_BUDGET_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_AUDIENCE_COUNT_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_GROUP_START_DATE_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_GROUP_END_DATE_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_GROUP_TOTAL_BUDGET_HOLD, CAMPAIGN_GROUP_STATUS_HOLD, ACCOUNT_SERVING_HOLD.

review.description: Creative review, read-only. Absent while the creative is in DRAFT (live responses also omit it on some REMOVED and CANCELED creatives). Documented status values: PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED, NEEDS_REVIEW. Not read by the product.

rejectionReasons.description: Rejection reason codes, from the page's rejection-reason list.

createdBy.description: Member URN that created the creative, urn:li:person:{id} (urn:li:unknown observed live). Captures redact it.

lastModifiedBy.description: Member URN that last modified the creative, urn:li:person:{id} (urn:li:unknown observed live). Captures redact it.

metadata.description: Cursor paging metadata. On the last page it is empty or carries a null nextPageToken.

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page, sent back as the pageToken query parameter. Absent or null on the last page.

paging.description: Legacy Rest.li collection paging block. The documented sample omits it, but live 202609 responses carry it on the last page (2026-10-07). Its count does not track the number of elements, and links can hold a stale rel=next href in the old start/count style even when no nextPageToken is present. Cursor search pages by metadata.nextPageToken only, so the client never reads this block; it is declared so real responses validate.
